task.title: Reviewing entitlement to Work-Sharing (WS) for the last week

step.cmd: Determine if one of the following conditions is met:

ul.li: The RFS is not contentious.

The RFS is allowed as just cause.
If one of the conditions is met, go to step 15.
If none of the conditions are met, the week before the week of the separation is processed as the last week of WS benefits. Go to step 18.

step.cmd: Determine if the client worked at least a half hour with the WS employer:

ul.li: If no, the week before the week in which the separation occurs is processed as the last week of WS benefits. Go to step 18.

If yes, determine if fact-finding with the client is required to obtain the following information:
What BT does the client want to receive for the week of the separation?
Any details required for claimant’s reports for the WS period that must be modified or that have not been received. Refer to Claimant’s report for more information.
If fact-finding is required, fact-find with the client and go to step 16. fact-find
If fact-finding is not required, go to step 18.
Claimant’s report

step.cmd: Determine if the client was contacted during fact-finding:

ul.li: If the client was contacted, go to step 17.
If the client was not contacted and did not reply to the N-10-00-00 letter, the week in which the separation occurs is processed as the last week of WS benefits. Go to step 18.

step.cmd: In NWS, add details to the draft SROC created during fact-finding or create a new SROC as follows:

ul.li: Main Issue: Select Other .
Comments: Type “Separation from WS employer during WS agreement.”
Details: Document the fact-finding details according to the National Fact-Finding and Documentation Policy . National Fact-Finding and Documentation Policy
Click Save.

step.cmd: Determine if this is a WS claim from the Western Canada and Territories region:

ul.li: If yes, go to step 19.
If no, go to step 23.

step.cmd: Determine if any of the following must be input or modified:

ul.li: The WS agreement end date (must equal the last week of WS benefits).

Claimant’s reports for WS benefits.
If any inputs or modifications are required, go to step 20.
If no inputs or modifications are required, refer to Conversion and renewal . Conversion and renewal

step.cmd: In NWS create an IPOC REV WI as follows:

ul.li: Complexity: Select Level 1 .
Language: Select the appropriate language.
Destination — SCC: Select 5903 Vancouver IPOC .
End User: Select Next available user .
Issue: Select Work-Sharing .
BPC: Type the BPC of the claim.
Comments: Type “Claimant’s report information for Work-Sharing period.”
Details: Type the agreement start and end date, and any claimant’s report information for the WS period that must be modified or that have not been input.
Obtained by: Select the appropriate method.
Obtained from: Select the appropriate source.
Source details: Enter the source details.
Click Save .

step.cmd: In NWS, move the WI to Pending as follows:

ul.li: Pending reason: Select Other .
Comments: Type “Awaiting processing of WS information and the claimant’s reports.”
Bring forward date: Enter today’s date + 2 days.

step.cmd: When the WI moves to the current workload, determine if the Project Data — Training (M171) transaction and the claimant’s report have been processed:

ul.li: If no, repeat step 21.
If yes, go to step 23.

step.cmd: In FTS, determine if the WS end week indicated on the claim is correct:

ul.li: If no, go to step 24.
If yes, go to Work-Sharing (WS) end week is correct . Work-Sharing (WS) end week is correct

step.cmd: Determine if the current WS end week is later than the correct WS end week:

ul.li: If yes, go to Current Work-Sharing (WS) end week is later than the correct WS end week . Current Work-Sharing (WS) end week is later than the correct WS end week
If no, go to Current Work-Sharing (WS) end week is not later than the correct WS end week . Current Work-Sharing (WS) end week is not later than the correct WS end week
